content_voiceover: Langerhans cell histiocytosis, or L C H, is defined as a clonal neoplasm arising from an immature dendritic cell, or in some cases from an earlier hematopoietic precursor cell. Pathologically, the diagnostic markers on immunohistochemistry are C D one a and C D two oh seven, also called langerin, which is the Langerhans cell antigen. On electron microscopy, the classic finding is Birbeck granules, which have a distinctive tennis racket shape. In terms of pathogenesis, this is a RAS RAF MEK ERK pathway disease, driven by B R A F V six hundred E mutations in fifty to sixty percent of cases, which activates that MAP kinase signaling cascade. For risk stratification, the critical distinction is risk organs versus not: the hematopoietic system, liver, spleen, and lung count as risk organs, and involvement here changes prognosis and treatment intensity. There's also a special site category covering vertebral lesions and CNS risk lesions, which need closer monitoring even without classic risk organ involvement, plus a category for organ dysfunction. Treatment depends entirely on which sites are involved, ranging from observation for a single lesion, to steroids, to systemic chemotherapy for multisystem or risk organ disease. The five year overall survival is good for low risk patients, meaning those without risk organ involvement, but worse for those with risk organ dysfunction at diagnosis.
keypoints: LCH: clonal dendritic cell neoplasm; IHC positive for CD1a and CD207 (langerin); EM shows Birbeck granules
Pathogenesis: BRAF V600E mutation in 50-60%, activating RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK pathway
Risk organs are hematopoietic system, liver, spleen, and lung; special sites include vertebral and CNS-risk lesions
Treatment and prognosis depend on site involvement; low-risk (no risk-organ) patients have good 5-year survival
keypoint_voiceover: L C H is a clonal dendritic cell neoplasm, positive for C D one a and C D two oh seven on immunohistochemistry, with Birbeck granules on electron microscopy. Roughly half to sixty percent have a B R A F V six hundred E mutation activating the RAS RAF MEK ERK pathway. Risk organs are hematopoietic system, liver, spleen, and lung, and their involvement drives both treatment intensity and prognosis.
